facts.text: Lidar snow models exist, including LISA and models by Teufel et al., but their validation is weaker than validation for fog.
facts.quote: Lidar snow models exist (LISA; Teufel et al.) with weaker validation than fog

facts.text: Published physically based work reports that synthetic snowfall and wet-ground effects can improve detection on real snowy data, mostly on automotive datasets.
facts.quote: published physically based work reports that synthetic snowfall and wet-ground effects can improve detection on real snowy data, mostly on automotive datasets

facts.text: Turbulent snow degraded all tested lidars in a 2019 chamber and field study.

facts.text: Radar snow attenuation was measured at 77 GHz in 2019.
facts.quote: Radar snow attenuation has been measured at 77 GHz (2019)

facts.text: Radar snow attenuation has less direct public validation than radar attenuation in rain or fog.
facts.quote: Radar snow attenuation has been measured at 77 GHz (2019), but there is less direct public validation than for rain or fog [42].

facts.text: Camera snow effects, including flakes and accumulation, are rated as needing scene understanding in the 2026 editing benchmark.

facts.text: There is little off-road evidence for camera snow effects, including flakes and accumulation.
